evidence.summary: CBS News reports U.S. officials say Iranian forces brought down at least two American MQ-1 unmanned aircraft in recent days. Location and MQ-1 variant were not disclosed. This materially changes the aircraft-loss drawer: at least two recent U.S. UAS losses now have U.S.-official-source corroboration, but the reported type is MQ-1, not MQ-9. Do not map these losses automatically to either Qeshm claim without location/time evidence. The distinction strengthens the pending Lie Ledger audit of IRGC claims that the Qeshm aircraft represented the 52nd/53rd U.S. MQ-9: Iran's public aggregate is not supported by this U.S. confirmation and appears to be conflating or relabeling aircraft types.
unresolved: Whether either MQ-1 loss corresponds to a Qeshm engagement

evidence.summary: Maritime Executive reports UKMTO described a tanker incident involving an unknown projectile while IRGC identified the Togo-flagged Trend and claimed it set the vessel ablaze and stopped its passage. This strengthens existence of a maritime attack/incident independent of the IRGC narrative but does not independently establish the weapon, claimed U.S. direction, or IRGC assertion of total control over Hormuz. Preserve 'total control' and destruction threats as separate propaganda/control propositions.
unresolved: Whether passage actually ceased because of the strike

evidence.summary: Reuters' field report states renewed fighting has forced more than 115,000 people from homes and reports an IOM figure of at least 112,000 internally displaced plus nearly 3,000 who fled to Djibouti by boat. This refines the prior 104,796 IOM DTM baseline while preserving the separate OCHA/aid-agency ~125,000/115,000 denominators rather than merging them.

Reuters reports Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto called for more naval assets to protect Red Sea navigation and said Italy is preparing an independent naval mission while criticizing delays in the EU Aspides response. This is a forward force-posture indicator, not evidence that additional ships are already deployed.

AP reports a new U.S. military estimate putting war cost at $43.6 billion as of Sep. 3, up $5.6 billion from early August, with weapons expenditures rising to $28.1 billion. AP also reports continuing concern over Patriot/THAAD interceptor depletion. Preserve cost date (Sep. 3) separately from publication date (Sep. 18).

AP reports Iran's largest government-organized rally since the war began, with more than 300,000 participants reported in Tehran. Iranian officials said more than 600,000 civilians had registered for military training and projected more than one million. Preserve the rally as independently observed/reported while keeping volunteer-registration totals as Iranian official claims unless independently audited.
unresolved: Actual training throughput and military utility

evidence.summary: AP reports the U.S. approved visas for President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to attend the UN General Assembly high-level meeting, with stringent travel/purchasing restrictions. This preserves a diplomatic channel/access point amid hostilities; it is not evidence of negotiations or concessions.
unresolved: Whether bilateral/mediated contacts occur in New York
